title: Graceful Handshake Reservation Proxy (GH-RP) — PRD (wip)
body:
Context
---
We keep seeing two recurring pain points from Dedicated customers: (1) spiky workloads that need short lived extra capacity but cannot tolerate wholesale model/fleet fallbacks, and (2) noisy tenants whose transient peak behavior degrades other customers despite quotaing. Current approaches (hard quotas, coarse burst credits, or aggressive preemption) are either too blunt or cause poor customer UX.

This doc proposes the Graceful Handshake Reservation Proxy (GH-RP), a mediation layer between the request router/autoscaler and dedicated capacity pools. GH-RP focuses on short-lived negotiated reservations, soft-fallbacks, and an isolation signal protocol that preserves latency SLOs while enabling elastic bursts with predictable economic accounting.

Goals (measurable)
- Reduce customer-observed burst-induced tail latency by 40% for customers using reservation-based bursts vs baseline hard-fallbacks.
- Enable 60% of transient peak requests to be served on dedicated capacity (via GH-RP) instead of falling back to hosted or degraded models.
- Keep eviction incidents caused by bursts under 0.1% of total requests per week across dedicated clusters.
- Provide clear billing/crediting visibility for burst reservations (per-request attribution).

Non-goals
- Replace long-running reserved capacity contracts or fundamental scheduling (this augments autoscaler and quota subsystems).
- Solve noisy neighbor problems originating from poorly designed customer workloads (we mitigate, but do not police application-level behavior).

User stories
- As an engineering customer, I want to request short-lived burst capacity for a campaign window with predictable cost and low risk of model degradation for my baseline requests.
- As a platform operator, I want a soft preemption protocol that minimizes cross-tenant P99 latency regressions and provides deterministic metrics for audits.
- As Redwood billing, I want per-reservation usage logs that map to surge credits and invoiceable events.

High-level approach
- Introduce a Reservation Proxy service (GH-RP) that exposes a small API to the request router and autoscaler. GH-RP manages: reservation tokens, handshake negotiation (grant/offer/commit), graceful downgrade tickets, and isolation signals.
- Reservations are short-lived (default TTL 5–20 minutes), priced via surge-credit consumption, and can be partially granted (pro-rated fulfillment) with explicit degradation lanes.
- The autoscaler and pool manager propagate current pool headroom to GH-RP. GH-RP computes provisional grants based on SLO-weighted utility (configurable per-customer).
- Request router attaches reservation-token to incoming requests; runtime enforces token-based fast-pathing and KV-cache affinity where available.

Core components and flow
1) Reservation Request: client (or customer-side control plane) requests N concurrency or X tokens for T minutes via GH-RP API. Request includes SLO weight and model fingerprint.
2) Offer Calculation: GH-RP queries pool headroom and active reservations; runs a quick utility function (see algorithm) that returns an offer: full, partial (percentage), or defer.
3) Client Accept/Commit: client can accept partial offer or wait/retry. On commit, GH-RP mints a reservation token with attributes (pool, model, allowed concurrency, token expiration).
4) Routing & Enforcement: router checks token and routes to dedicated pool in fast-path, enforcing concurrency clamps. If pool cannot honor at point of routing, runtime may issue a soft downgrade (see fallback ticket) to the router.
5) Reconciliation & Billing: GH-RP emits per-token usage events to billing and observability.

Reservation semantics and controls
- Soft Grants: grants that can be partially rescinded with a minimum notice window (default 30s). Rescinds result in downgrade tickets and optional fallback to hosted model.
- Graceful Handshake: a two-stage commit: (a) provisional grant (reserves resources logically), (b) final commit when client starts using tokens. This avoids over-reservation and supports rapid churn.
- Quota Translation: map account-level quotas into reservation caps; GH-RP enforces both account quota and pool-based caps.
- Burst Degradation Lanes: defined degradation paths (e.g., reduced max tokens, model quantized variant, degraded sequence length) with priority ranking; chosen by GH-RP when partial grant required.

Autoscaling & algorithm (sketch)
- Inputs: pool_capacity, current_tail_latency(SLO window), active_reservations, ambient_traffic_forecast (short-horizon), per-customer SLO weight.
- Score function: utility = weight * (expected_revenue_per_request) - penalty(latency_impact, eviction_risk)
- Offer rules:
  - If utility > threshold and headroom >= min_reserve => full grant
  - If headroom < min_reserve but utility still positive => partial grant scaled by headroom
  - If granting causes modeled p99 delta > configured limit => either deny or offer degradation lane
- Credit accounting: each grant consumes surge credits at grant-time (prepay) or at use-time (postpay) depending on customer preference. Prepay preferred for predictable quotas.

Isolation signal protocol
- GH-RP emits structured isolation signals to pool scheduler to indicate: reservation_id, soft_expiry, priority_score, and allowed_eviction_sensitivity.
- Scheduler uses these signals to prefer evicting opportunistic workloads over committed reservations.
- Retry/backoff policy: clients receive a handshake-state header; on soft rescind, clients can retry with exponential backoff + optional fallback flag.

Operational controls & UI
- Console surfaces: reservation request composer, outstanding reservations list (with expiration and consumed credits), per-reservation latency and success rate.
- Admin toggles: global max burst window, per-tenant max reservation cap, emergency preemption toggle.
- Alerts: high rescind rate, reservation-request queue growth, mismatches between promised vs served tokens.

Metrics to track
- Reservation success rate (requests served with token / total reservation requests)
- Burst fulfillment fraction (tokens actually served / tokens committed)
- P99 delta attributed to bursts (before vs after reservation grants)
- Eviction incidents attributable to GH-RP rescinds
- Billing accuracy gaps (invoices vs token-usage logs)

Rollout plan (phases)
- Phase 0 (lab): simulator for GH-RP logic against historical workload traces (2 weeks). Create a model of headroom and synthetic offers.
- Phase 1 (internal): soft launch for Redwood internal teams + one low-risk customer, monitoring with canary configs (1 month). Policy set conservative: mostly partial grants, long notice windows.
- Phase 2 (opt-in beta): expose GH-RP to selected customers, enable prepay surge credits, add UI in console (2 months).
- Phase 3 (general availability): full feature with standard defaults, rollback hooks, and audit logs.

Open questions / tradeoffs
- Prepay vs postpay economics: prepay reduces billing complexity but may be a friction for customers. Which should be default? (Ops + Billing to decide)
- Minimum notice window for soft rescinds: 30s default feels ok but could be insufficient for some latency-sensitive apps. Should be customer-configurable?
- Where to implement handshake enforcement: router (fast path) vs runtime (slower but authoritative)? We probably need both - router for fast gating, runtime for final enforcement.

Immediate next steps / TODOs
- Build simulator (ENG-applied-ml + infra) to test score function against last 6 months of dedicated pool traces (owner: Jasper).
- Write a small routing header prototype (router team) to carry reservation-token metadata (owner: Elena).
- Billing schema proposal for surge credits and per-token events (owner: Priya).
- Draft runbook for soft rescind incidents and SRE response playbook.

Notes / links
- Early discussion Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C0ABC1234/p169...
- Related ideas: ad-hoc "safety pocket" feature (see JIRA-4301) and the preemptible backfill work.

Appendix: short handshake example
- Customer A requests 500 token-minutes for 10 minutes at weight=1.2. GH-RP inspects pool headroom (800 token-minutes available) and offers full grant. Customer commits and GH-RP mints reservation_id=R-20251108-41. Router uses R-... header and routes fast-path. After 6 minutes, pool pressure spikes from an unrelated job; GH-RP soft-rescinds 40% of outstanding capacity with 45s notice and offers quantized model variant lane. Customer chooses to accept quantized lane for remainder; billing logs reflect mixed usage.

This is a working draft — expect iteration. Comments inline are welcome; please add TODOs under the "Open questions" section in replies rather than editing the doc directly.
